config.winefoxs_spellbooks.show_maid_man: Shows an arc-shaped mana bar beside your own maids on the spell attack or spell support task. It fades out once their mana is full. Only affects this client; summoned maids are not shown.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.max_spell_ran: How far a maid searches for hostile targets. Anything beyond this is never picked. Larger values cost more scanning each tick.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.start_spell_r: A maid closes to this distance before it starts casting. Individual spells can set their own start casting range under Spell Compatibles.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.max_mana_mult: Maximum mana multiplier, relative to the player's (Default: 1)
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.battle_walk_s: Movement speed multiplier for strafing and repositioning during spell combat.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.max_combo_del: Maximum wait in ticks between two consecutive casts. Lower values make a maid chain spells more tightly.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.spell_plannin: Maids pick attack spells to take down the current target as fast as possible, using spell damage they learn and keep correcting from their own casts. They may save mana for a stronger spell instead of always spamming the cheapest one. Disable to restore the old uniform-random pick.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.drink_potion_: Unlimited healing potions in spell battle (Default: false)
A maid below 60% health drinks a healing potion without consuming an item, and can drink again as soon as the cooldown elapses — effectively unlimited sustain in combat.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.show_chat_bub: Show spell names in spell battle (Default: true)
Shows the name of the spell a maid is casting in her chat bubble. Useful for spectating and troubleshooting.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.melee_attack_: Allow maids to use melee weapons during spell attacks (Default: true)
When off, maids on the Magic Attack task only cast and never fall back to melee weapons.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.air_force_bas: Base chance for air force maid (Default: 0.1)
Base chance for each summoned maid to ride a broom. Added to the per-level chance below.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.air_force_cha: Extra flight chance added per level of the summoning spell, on top of the base chance.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.air_force_fol: How far above its summoner a flying maid keeps station.
Horizontal radius at which a flying maid circles its summoner.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.air_force_fly: Movement speed of a maid piloting a broom.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.air_force_min: A flying maid keeps at least this far from its target, backing off before casting instead of hovering right on top of it.

config.winefoxs_spellbooks.summoned_maid: Power caps for summoned maids, used to rein in what their randomly rolled loadouts can reach.
Highest spell level a summoned maid may carry (Default: 3)
Combined with the per-tier cap from the loadout datapack by taking the lower of the two — it can only reduce, never raise. Set to 10 to disable.
Highest spell rarity a summoned maid may carry (Default: EPIC)

Spells that exceed this rarity at every level are dropped from the pools entirely; the rest are levelled down until they fit. Filtering happens before rolling, so the number of spells a maid receives is unchanged. Set to LEGENDARY to disable.
Allow summoned maids to carry learned-only school spells, i.e. Eldritch (Default: false)
Learned-only schools — today, Eldritch — normally require a player to learn them first. Turning this on lets summoned maids roll them, bypassing that gate.
Creepers flee from summoned maids (Default: true)

Adds one AI goal to every creeper in the world. The goal costs nothing in dimensions with no summoned maid — it checks an O(1) counter before doing any entity search — so leaving this on is cheap. Turn it off to skip attaching the goal entirely.
config.winefoxs_spellbooks.lightning_man: Lightning-struck maids regenerate mana 100x faster (Default: false)
"Struck by lightning" is a permanent flag saved on the maid — once set it never wears off. With this on, such maids refill their whole mana bar every half second, which is effectively unlimited mana.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.summon_maid.gu: Summon mana-wielding maids to fight at your side for ten minutes. Higher levels call forth more maids.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.crescent_brand: Brands a single enemy with a crescent mark, leaving them vulnerable to further Vulpine interactions.
Brand a single enemy with a crescent mark. Any Vulpine damage detonates it, blasting nearby foes — detonations by your own maids hit harder and can chain.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.foxshade_wisps: Recast to loose one homing foxfire wisp per cast, up to 3. Each wisp flanks in and deals Vulpine damage, setting off any Crescent Brand it lands on.
Recast to loose homing foxfire wisps that flank your target from either side; every wisp deals Vulpine damage and detonates a Crescent Brand on impact.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.foxshade_ambus: Instant self-buff: coil for an ambush. The next time you deal damage to a foe, a foxshade appears nearby, dashes in and leaps to bite it once, then the effect fades.

Cast to coil for an ambush (10s). The next time you or your maid strikes a foe, a foxshade lands nearby, sprints to the target and leaps to bite it, dealing Vulpine damage and able to detonate a Crescent Brand — then the effect fades.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.crescent_mantl: Veil yourself and nearby owned maids in a crescent shroud: absorption hearts and brief invisibility to slip out of danger.
Veil yourself and your nearby maids in a crescent shroud, granting absorption and brief invisibility to slip out of danger.
spell.winefoxs_spellbooks.decant_the_bin: Pour off the dregs: harmful effects on you or a maid in your gaze are halved — or purged entirely at high vintage.
Pour off the dregs: shorten the harmful effects on yourself or an owned maid in your gaze — purged outright at full vintage.

patchouli.touhou_little_maid.book.catego: Winefox's Spellbooks is an addon for Iron's Spells and Spellbooks, adding spellcasting tasks for maids
patchouli.touhou_little_maid.book.entrie: Mod Introduction

A crossover between $(thing)Touhou Little Maid$() and $(thing)Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks$(): hand a maid a spellbook and she becomes a real spellcaster — she picks spells to suit the moment, budgets her mana, respects cooldowns, repositions, and plays a casting animation on GeckoLib models.
Beyond that it adds $(thing)Vulpine$(), a spell school of its own, built around $(bold)player and maid fighting as one$(): you brand, she detonates, and both of you are paid for it.

It also ships behaviour classifications for $(thing)several hundred spells$() across every supported Iron's Spells addon. Installed addons take effect automatically; addons you do not have cause no errors at all.$(br)Everything past the spellcasting maid is optional — the mod works fine without any of it.
Casting Media
A maid's $(thing)main hand, armour slots, accessory slots and Curios slots$() are all scanned; spells in any spell container — a spellbook, an imbued weapon, imbued armour — enter her spell list.
Only $(thing)one spellbook$() takes effect at a time, same as for players; imbued gear is not subject to that limit and stacks.$(br)Maids cannot cast from spell scrolls.

Spell level = the spell's own level + the Affinity bonus from her gear. Any change of equipment recalculates her spell list at once, and after $(thing)/reload$() updates the spell tags, loaded maids rescan as well.$(br)$(bold)A spell that belongs to no behaviour category is ignored$() — the most common reason for "she just won't cast that spell".
Mana

Just like players, mana is the key to maid spellcasting: different spells and levels cost different amounts. Equipping staves and mage armour raises her maximum mana, and the $(thing)Maximum mana multiplier$() option scales the whole bar.
A maid's mana bar is $(thing)independent of yours$(). Point at her with Jade to read it.
Natural regeneration defaults to roughly $(thing)2%% per second$(), scaled by mana regeneration attributes from her gear.

Having been struck by lightning is a $(thing)permanent$() flag saved on the maid — one strike and it never wears off. With $(thing)Lightning-struck maids regenerate mana 100x faster$() enabled, such maids refill the whole bar every 0.5 seconds. That option is $(bold)off by default$().
New Task Modes

This mod adds two new tasks for maids: Magic Attack and Magic Support.$(br)In Magic Attack mode, the maid will actively cast spells to attack hostile mobs. If she has a melee weapon and is close enough to the enemy, she will also use melee attacks.

In Magic Support mode, the maid will not actively attack enemies, but instead try to heal nearby injured masters and allied creatures (including maids with the same master), or provide buffs to allies and debuffs to enemies.

Her spell list is split into $(thing)seven behaviour categories$(): Attack, Defense, Movement, Self-heal, Negative Effect, Ally Buff and Ally Heal. Magic Attack uses the first five; Magic Support uses Defense, Self-heal, Negative Effect, Ally Buff and Ally Heal.$(br)Two further $(thing)markers$() take no part in classification: Summon and Recast.
Both tasks unlock the same way: an imbued weapon or armour, or a spellbook with inscribed spells in an accessory slot.

She decides every short interval ($(thing)Max combo delay tick$(), 10 by default): first she drops what she cannot cast — short on mana or still on cooldown — and finishes any unfinished multi-cast spell. Then she weights the categories her task allows, picks one by weighted random, and picks a spell inside it.

A dying ally outranks everything else. When a nearby ally needs help the support categories take priority and combat ones sit it out; otherwise she fights as usual; the lower her own health, the higher Defense and Movement; with no line of sight she rarely picks attack spells and repositions instead. An ally missing a buff, or carrying a cleansable debuff, lifts that spell's weight sharply.

Defense and Negative Effect both lose weight if she picked them last round, so she does not spam one category.$(br)In a fight she backs off when the target gets inside half her range, circles in place while in range and in sight, walks slower while casting, and stops repositioning entirely once told to sit.

Her search radius is $(thing)Maximum spell attack search range$() (64 by default), and branded enemies are preferred; she closes to $(thing)Start spell casting range$() (15 by default) before casting.
Casting Animation

This mod adapts casting animations for GeckoLib maid models. Model pack authors can create an animation/<packname>.iss.animation.json file to implement custom animations. For reference on default animation key names, see this file: $(l:https://github.com/TartaricAcid/TouhouLittleMaid/blob/1.21/src/main/resources/assets/touhou_little_maid/animation/iss.animation.json)Click to open$(/l)
Mod Integration

$(thing)Curios$() — a spellbook goes in the spellbook slot Iron's Spells defines, and a maid wears at most one; $(thing)Accessories$() works as an alternative.$(br)$(thing)Jade$() — point at a maid to read her mana; point at a summoned maid to also see her spell count, and hold Shift for the full list.

$(thing)JEI$() — every item this mod adds carries an info page; click the $(bold)i$() in the top right corner.$(br)$(thing)Advanced Loot Info$() — the loot this mod injects into chests, and the maid morning gift, both show their odds inside JEI, EMI or REI.$(br)All of these are optional.
Troubleshooting
$(bold)She does not cast at all.$() Check in order:

$(li)Task set to Magic Attack or Magic Support?$(li)Spellbook in an accessory slot, spell slots inscribed?$(li)$(bold)Does the spell have a behaviour tag?$() Spells outside every category are ignored.$(li)Mana enough, cooldown over?$(li)Enemy beyond her search range, or not yet in casting range?

$(bold)Her AoE spells keep hitting allies.$() Remove that spell's Attack category under Spell Compatibles and restart, or remove it from its behaviour tag with a datapack and run /reload.$(br)$(bold)My config change did nothing.$() Changes under Spell Compatibles need a game restart; datapack-side changes only need /reload.

$(bold)Why won't maids cast Summon Maid?$() By design — that spell is reserved for players.$(br)$(bold)My support maid never heals.$() Magic Support only acts on same-team targets, and she needs spells in the Ally Heal or Ally Buff categories.
Vulpine School

$(bold)Vulpine$() is the new spell school added by this mod, covering summoning, support and mana manipulation.$(br)The school is resolved by its own $(thing)spell power$() and $(thing)magic resist$() attributes, and stacks with mage gear bonuses from Iron's Spells itself.
It is designed for $(thing)player and maid together$(): you brand, your maid follows up and detonates, and the mantle and cleanse you cast also cover nearby maids.
While a target is branded, the moment it takes any $(thing)Vulpine damage$() the brand detonates into a school AoE burst; burst damage = $(thing)a base of 10$() plus the spell power at branding time.

Detonated by a $(thing)player$(): radius 3, no chaining. Detonated by $(thing)your own maid$(): x1.5 damage, radius 4 (5 at full Brewsurge on the owner), and the burst can chain-detonate the next branded target.$(br)A brand left to expire on its own only pops weakly within 2 blocks: 3 points of plain magic damage, no chaining.

$(bold)Brewsurge$() is the school's shared buff: every detonation — by you or by your own maid — stacks one level on the commander (rolling 10-second refresh, up to 3 stacks), each granting +10%% Vulpine spell power. A brand that expires on its own grants none.
$(bold)Tipsy$() deals no damage, but it slows movement by 30%%, makes victims stagger and wander, and badly deflects any arrows they loose. Your own maids are immune to the mist and the wine pools.
School Items
Vulpine Anima

The school's Focus — a lively wisp of foxfire coils within the glass orb.$(br)At the $(thing)Scroll Forge$() it is the crafting ingredient for this school's spell scrolls, and it doubles as a casting implement for higher-tier spells.
$(bold)Vulpine Anima$() is obtained from:

$(li)Max-favorability maid's morning gift (95%%)$(li)Fairies your maids kill: tamed 25%%, summoned 35%%, +5%% per Looting level$(li)Chests: woodland mansion 25%%, nether fortress 20%%, stronghold library 15%%$(li)Iron's Spells: Pyromancer Tower, Catacombs, Citadel library
Crescent Blood Vintage

A vintage sealed under a waning crescent. Drinkable.$(br)A $(thing)maid$() who drinks it always gains $(thing)Foxfire Boost$() for 10 seconds. $(thing)Anyone else$() risks Nausea, Poison and Mana Disruption — 60%% each, rolled separately.

$(bold)Crescent Blood Vintage$() is found in chests:$(li)Village houses 20%%, village temple 25%%$(li)Pillager outpost 30%%$(li)Woodland mansion 40%%$(li)Iron's Spells: Pyromancer Tower casks up to 50%%, plus the Citadel, Catacombs, Ice Spider Den, Impaled Icebreaker and Mangrove Hut

$(bold)Foxfire Boost$() cuts new cooldowns to about 10%% of normal, and the moment it is applied it also shortens every cooldown already running by 90%%. Ten seconds is enough for a maid to empty her whole spell list.
$(bold)Mana Disruption$() blocks all mana regeneration outright — natural regen, wine pools, everything — and drains a further 1%% of maximum mana every half second.

$(bold)Vulpine scrolls$() are how the school is learned. Craft them at Iron's Spells' $(thing)Scroll Forge$() with $(thing)Vulpine Anima$() as the Focus, then write the scroll into a spell book at an $(thing)Inscription Table$(), or imbue it into a weapon or armour piece.$(br)Maids read the book, never the scroll.

Ready-made school scrolls also turn up in chests: stronghold library 20%%, nether fortress 15%%, and Iron's Spells' Catacombs coffins 25%%, Citadel tomes 30%%, Pyromancer Tower old casks 30%%.$(br)This mod's own creative tab holds both items plus every level of every school scroll.
School Spells
Crescent Brand

$(thing)Level 1-8, 10s cooldown, Negative Effect.$()$(br)A ray marks a single target up to 16 blocks away with a Crescent Brand: 12 seconds, +1s per level.$(br)The brand deals no damage itself — it is a fuse waiting to be lit, and detonating it is what the rest of the school is for.
Foxshade Wisps

$(thing)Level 3-8, 15s cooldown, Attack.$()$(br)A recast spell: the first cast pays the mana, then each further press looses one homing wisp, up to 3 in total; letting 4 seconds lapse ends the volley into cooldown.

Each wisp locks onto a hostile target within 16 blocks and flanks in from the side, dealing Vulpine damage equal to twice your school spell power and setting off any Crescent Brand it lands on. All three are identical — there is no finisher shot. Maids on Magic Attack chain the recasts automatically.
Foxshade Ambush

$(thing)Level 1-4, 8s cooldown, Defense.$()$(br)Spends its mana up front and does nothing visible: it marks you for 10 seconds. The next time you deal $(thing)any$() damage to a hostile mob, a foxshade lands nearby, sprints in and pounces once — then the mark is spent.
Only hostile mobs arm it, and not one that is airborne or has no ground to land on. Bite damage scales with spell power, so cast it before the opening blow.
Crescent Mantle

$(thing)Level 3-8, 30s cooldown, Defense.$()$(br)Veils you and every owned maid within 6 blocks in $(thing)Absorption II$() (4 seconds base, upgraded to Absorption III from level 6) plus $(thing)True Invisibility$() (3 seconds base — gear vanishes too and mobs lose aggro). Both durations gain +0.5s per level.
When focused down, mantle up, slip away, then decide whether to counterattack or retreat.
Decant the Bind

$(thing)Level 2-5, 20s cooldown, Self-heal.$()$(br)The school's cleanse: it targets yourself, or an owned maid in your gaze within 16 blocks.$(br)On cast, every harmful effect on the target has its remaining duration halved; at max level (5) they are purged outright instead.
Tipsy Mist
$(thing)Level 1-8, 12s cooldown, Negative Effect.$()$(br)Rolls out a plum-pink fog, 5 blocks in radius, at the aimed spot (up to 24 blocks away), lasting 6 seconds plus 0.5s per level.
Creatures inside are repeatedly doused with $(thing)Tipsy$(); your own maids stroll through unbothered. From spell level 5 it applies Tipsy II, doubling the slow and the stagger.
Vintner's Bomb

$(thing)Level 1-8, 8s cooldown, Attack.$()$(br)Hurls a bottle of crescent vintage: a direct hit deals Vulpine damage, and the impact spreads a $(thing)wine pool$() 2.5 blocks in radius that lasts 5 seconds.$(br)Foes soaking in the pool are kept Tipsy; your own maids soak up mana instead, about 5%% of their maximum per second.
Mana Transfer

$(thing)Level 1-10, 15s cooldown, Ally Buff.$()$(br)A continuous spell, lasting up to 5 seconds and channelling the caster's mana to the aimed target. The target must be a $(thing)player$() or an entity with a mana pool, such as this mod's maids.
It costs about 20%% more mana than it delivers, and higher levels deliver more per second. Maids on Magic Support cast it on allies whose mana is low.
Summon Maid

$(thing)Level 1-6, 150s cooldown.$()$(br)Summons a squad of temporary maids for 10 minutes: two of them at level 1, up to seven at level 6, and more still with school spell power gear. $(bold)Maids never cast this spell themselves$() — it is reserved for players.
Casting it again while the squad is out does not add another squad; it dismisses the existing one early.$(br)What the squad can actually do follows.
Summoned Maids
Summoned maids are temporary combat units. Each rolls a model at random, and rolls gear and spells by summon level, then automatically takes a Magic Attack or Magic Support task.

They $(bold)cannot be interacted with, take no orders and never sit$(); they simply fight alongside the summoner. They $(bold)drop no gear on death$() and vanish when their time runs out. By default creepers actively avoid them.

Three built-in loadouts, each with its own gear and spell mix:$(br)$(li)$(bold)Warrior$() — mostly attack spells, the heaviest armour, never rides$(li)$(bold)Mage$() — attack and negative effect, some defense and movement, may ride$(li)$(bold)Support$() — healing and buffs for the summoner and the squad

How often each turns up is a weight: $(bold)warrior$() 40, $(bold)mage$() 35, $(bold)support$() 25.$(br)Every loadout has three tiers keyed to summon level — 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6. The higher the tier, the more complete the armour, the more spells, and the higher the spell level cap.
Some maids ride a $(thing)broom$() into the air and cast while circling above the summoner; the chance rises with summon level.
Point at a summoned maid with $(thing)Jade$() to see her mana and her spell count; hold Shift for the full spell list.

Two server options cap what they may carry: $(thing)Highest spell level$() (3 by default) and $(thing)Highest spell rarity$() (Epic by default). Both only ever reduce what a loadout offers, never raise it. Learned-only school spells such as Eldritch are excluded unless you enable them.
Datapack Customisation
Which spells a maid may cast is decided by $(thing)spell tags$(). To ban one — a friendly-fire heavy AoE, say — remove it from its tag with a datapack, then run /reload.
The behaviour tags live under $(thing)data/<namespace>/tags/irons_spellbooks/spells/$(). Config can also add or remove spells; it applies after the tags and wins where the two conflict.

The nine files there are $(thing)attack_spells$(), $(thing)defense_spells$(), $(thing)movement_spells$(), $(thing)support_spells$() (self-heal), $(thing)positive_effect_spells$() (ally buff), $(thing)negative_effect_spells$(), $(thing)support_effect_spells$() (ally heal), plus the markers $(thing)summon_spells$() and $(thing)maid_should_recast_spells$().

$(thing)data/<namespace>/magic_maid_spell_data/$() overrides per-spell metadata: the start casting range of a spell, and which mob effect that spell applies — so she can tell whether an ally still needs the buff.
Both have config equivalents under Spell Compatibles, but those need a game restart while the datapack only needs /reload, and config entries win where the two overlap.

Summoned maid loadouts are fully datapack-driven, at $(thing)data/<namespace>/summoned_maid_loadouts/<name>.json$().$(br)Each file defines a weight, a model filter, a broom mode, and tiered equipment and spell pools keyed by summon level. Weapons and armour are referenced via item tags, spells via spell tags, all supporting weighted randomisation and roll count ranges.

See the built-in warrior.json, mage.json and support.json for reference.$(br)The morning gift is itself a loot table, $(thing)winefoxs_spellbooks:gameplay/maid_morning_gift$(), so a pack can make a maid hand over something else entirely.
Commands and Config

Both commands require permission level 2.$(br)$(thing)/wsb cast <targets> <spell> [level]$() makes the given entities cast a spell, level 1-10. It only skips the pre-cast availability checks and $(bold)still consumes mana$(), so raise the target's mana cap before testing.
$(thing)/wsb summon [target] [count] [summonLevel] [loadout] [duration] [airForce]$() — with no arguments it summons for yourself. Duration is in seconds, -1 for permanent.
Everything is $(thing)server config$(); in multiplayer the server's settings win. Edit it from the mod list config screen.
